subject: Usage spike reconciliation & settlement proposal — Curium Health
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@curiumhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Zhou <michael.zhou@curiumhealth.com>; procurement@curiumhealth.com
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected May overage — can we reconcile?

Hi Monica,

We noticed a significant jump in usage for May on our platform account (DEAL-8472) after the team rolled the new conversation templates live on May 12. The spike shows up as ~1.8x token consumption vs. our historical baseline and produced an overage charge we weren't expecting.

Attached is an export from our side (curium_usage_export_may.csv) with the timeframe and sample request IDs. Can Redwood help reconcile where the extra tokens came from and propose a one-time settlement? Procurement will need a short write-up for their records if we agree to any credit.

Thanks — Elena

--
Elena Park
Head of Product Ops, Curium Health
elena.park@curiumhealth.com
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@curiumhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected May overage — can we reconcile?

Hi Elena — thanks for flagging this and for the CSV. We’ll investigate immediately.

Plan / next steps:
- Ben (cc) will pull the server-side token breakdown and a per-endpoint request log for May 1–31.
- Rachel (cc) will confirm the invoiced overage line and the suggested accounting approach for a credit.
- I’ll follow up within 48 hours with a proposed settlement and a short note you can send to procurement.

Can you confirm the account timezone and whether the sample request IDs in your CSV are from the production project (curium-prod) or a staging key? That will speed reconciliation.

Best,
Monica
Director, Commercial 
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Curium — draft settlement parameters

Folks — I pulled the logs. Quick summary:
- Confirmed production key (curium-prod) used after May 12 rollout.
- Net extra tokens (May 12–31) = 2,476,900 tokens. Invoiced overage amount = $9,908.
- Root cause: average system prompt length increased due to a new health summary step that concatenates clinical notes; was not batched/trimmed in the new template.

Proposed customer-facing settlement (draft):
1) One-time credit = 65% of invoiced overage ($6,441) applied to the June invoice, to help them through the rollout gap.
2) Offer a temporary committed capacity top-up: 20% capacity increase for the next 3 months at a reduced unit rate (15% off) if they sign an amendment (DEAL-8472-A).
3) Provide a short root-cause writeup + remediation steps for procurement.

I attached a quick credit memo draft (credit_memo_draft_453.pdf) and the raw usage breakdown. If approved by Karthik and finance we can send to Elena.

Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Curium — draft settlement parameters

Ben — thanks for the analysis. Notes from pricing/finance: 
- 65% is generous for a first-time operational spike. Recommend we standardize to 50% credit to keep precedent manageable.
- Approve the 3-month top-up offer but require the amendment to include: committed baseline increase, start/end dates, and explicit rollback language after the 3 months.
- Finance needs the invoice numbers to apply the credit properly (please include original invoice ID and the month it covers).

If everyone agrees, send the 50% credit + top-up offer to the customer with the Draft Settlement Terms attached and a DocuSign link for the amendment. We can escalate if procurement pushes back.

Karthik
Head of Commercial Strategy, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@curiumhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed settlement for May overage (DEAL-8472)

Elena — thank you for your patience. Attached are two artifacts: 1) a Redwood view of the May usage by endpoint (usage_report_redwood_view.csv) and 2) a short Draft Settlement Terms document (settlement_terms_draft.pdf) you can share with procurement.

Our proposed resolution: 
- Redwood will apply a one-time credit equal to 50% of the invoiced overage ($4,954) to your June invoice (invoice INV-20260531-8472).
- We’ll provide an optional committed capacity top-up: +20% baseline for 3 months at a 15% reduced unit rate. This will be added via an amendment (DEAL-8472-A).
- We’ll include a one-page remediation summary describing the token source and recommended prompt trimming; Ben will own implementation verification.

If this looks acceptable, I’ve added a DocuSign link here for the amendment: https://docusign.example.com/AAu1b2c3d4. Once we have a signed amendment, finance will schedule the credit to apply to the June invoice.

If procurement needs different phrasing, send their redlines and we’ll move quickly.

Best,
Monica
From: Elena Park <elena.park@curiumhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Zhou <michael.zhou@curiumhealth.com>; procurement@curiumhealth.com
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed settlement for May overage (DEAL-8472)

Monica — this looks reasonable, thank you. Procurement asked for the following additions before signing: 
- A single-line invoice credit description that we can attach to our PO ("Redwood overage credit — May 2026, INV-20260531-8472").
- Confirmation that the top-up pricing will be fixed for the 3-month period and will revert automatically at month-end.

We will sign the amendment once those two items are in the DocuSign package. I’ve looped in procurement and Michael.

Elena
